normal_exactly_one_contract: First ball inside current rigid 40–41mm envelope arrives and is parked.
Actual four followers satisfy the budget and cannot override a blocked gate.
Fresh ready and downstream-clear conditions allow commitment.
User completes pull; actual ball progresses forward to downstream trip in finite time.
While held, rear remains closed; only full released reset rearms.
necessary_load_conditions: Ball-induced radial feeler force must exceed feeler spring + slide friction + sear release force.
Unloaded air/turbulence/acceleration must not trip the ready or exit sensor.
Pawl reaction goes to fixed housing; user force must not pass through sphere or sensing plunger.
Available forward force must exceed sensor resistance, existing friction and spin load; fixed fan speed alone supplies no numerical lower bound.
A fresh downstream outward trip certifies clearance at that instant; arbitrary reverse motion before front closure is not covered without a separate one-way restraint.
limits: No CAD, assembled collision check, actual spring selection, printed fit or force validation for this proposal.
The existing1mm full mechanical error budget has not yet been certified.
A blocked or starved mechanism may stop; that is abnormal containment, not claimed successful one-ball output.
No source file in the frozen assembly was edited.

ordinary_point_shot_scope.definition: One ball already loaded; full pull; held trigger does not refill; ball clears before full reset. Empty pull and partial reversal are separate optional fault-tolerance features, not inherent violations of ordinary point-shot operation.
ordinary_point_shot_scope.at_least_one_successful_exit_requires: Finite forward progress against all drag; not established by fixed fan speed alone.

recommendation: Do not integrate three new interlocks as a mandatory change to this normal-point-shot version. If extra anti-partial-cycle behavior is desired, first model only the external full-stroke direction latch; occupancy/departure hardware remains an optional separate development with additional drag and force requirements.
